title: Quickstart templates (RAG + agents) — project overview
author: Talia Benson
body:
## Summary
Redwood Inference is shipping a set of **production-minded Quickstart templates** that take a developer from “API key” → a working, observable application quickly, without teaching unsafe patterns.

These templates are intended to be:
- **Fast to run locally** (<15 minutes to first successful run).
- **Straightforward to deploy** (<60 minutes to a managed environment with Docker/Kubernetes).
- **Operationally sane by default** (timeouts, retries/backoff, health checks, graceful shutdown, structured logs, OpenTelemetry tracing/metrics).
- **Aligned with Redwood Console** (token-level cost breakdowns, route/model tagging, error taxonomy, trace exemplars).

This page is the single overview for: goals, template catalog (v1), owners/DRIs, success metrics, and how each template maps to Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment modes.

---

## Goals (what success looks like)
### Primary goals
1) **Reduce time-to-first-success** for PLG users.
- Target: **<15 minutes** to first successful run.
- Target: **<60 minutes** to a deployed environment (container or minimal k8s).

2) Provide “**production shape**” from day one.
- Sane config layering, health checks, graceful shutdown.
- Observability hooks (traces, metrics, logs) and baseline dashboards/alerts.
- Guardrails to avoid common support ticket drivers (streaming disconnects, missing retries/timeouts, noisy logs, confusing 429 behavior).

3) Establish a **stable template contract** across languages.
- Consistent env var naming.
- Consistent telemetry schema (trace attrs, metric names, log fields).
- Consistent error codes/classes.

4) Improve **supportability** and reduce repetitive onboarding issues.
- Standard error taxonomy and remediation links.
- Known issues + workarounds documented and kept current.

### Non-goals
- Building a new framework or managed agent runtime.
- Supporting every vector DB / tool plugin out of the gate.
- Writing “toy demos” that do not model production concerns.

---

## Template catalog (v1)
All templates are shipped in **redwood-quickstarts** with language-specific implementations and a shared “contract” (env vars, telemetry, error taxonomy).

> Note: The detailed feature/back-end support matrix is maintained on the Template catalog & support matrix page.

### Catalog overview
| Template | Primary use case | Default backend(s) | Languages (v1) | Deploy paths | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RAG service + ingestion pipeline | “Search my docs” / knowledge base Q&A | One default vector DB backend + adapter interface | Python (FastAPI), TypeScript (Node) | Local, Docker Compose, minimal k8s | Includes ingestion worker; caching defaults; retrieval eval hooks |
| Agents (tool calling) | Workflow orchestration with safe tool usage | Tool allow-list + timeout wrappers | Python, TypeScript | Local, Docker Compose, minimal k8s | JSON schema validation for tool I/O; safe error handling |
| RAG + agent combined | Support-agent / ticket assistant | Retrieval as a tool + planner/executor | Python, TypeScript | Local, Docker Compose, minimal k8s | Includes prompt-injection and tool misuse guardrails; optional eval runner config |

### What every template includes (required)
**Operational defaults**
- Request timeouts (client + server), retries/backoff where safe, and circuit-breaker style protections.
- Health endpoints and readiness/liveness probes (where applicable).
- Graceful shutdown and in-flight request handling.

**Observability**
- OpenTelemetry traces with required attributes.
- Cost/latency metrics and error taxonomy.
- Structured JSON logs with request/tenant correlation IDs.

**Security baseline**
- Secrets management guidance (no keys committed; safe .env usage; CI secret scanning expectations).
- Tool calling safety (allow-lists; timeouts; schema validation; safe failure modes).
- PII guidance (what not to log; redaction note; data retention pointers).

## Success metrics (launch gates + ongoing tracking)
### Activation / onboarding metrics
Measured from docs + template instrumentation (where possible).
- **First call success rate** (Hosted API): target >= 90% within 24 hours of key creation.
- **Time-to-first-success**: median < 15 minutes (tracked via self-reported + telemetry events in template runs where applicable).
- **Template completion funnel**: clone → configure → run → first successful response → first deploy.

### Reliability / supportability metrics
- **Support ticket rate per template run**: reduce top drivers (429 confusion, timeouts on ingestion, streaming disconnects).
- **Template smoke test pass rate (CI):** target >= 99% on main.
- **Error taxonomy coverage:** >= 95% of surfaced errors map to a documented error class with remediation steps.

### Observability adoption metrics
- % of deployed template instances emitting:
  - required trace attributes
  - token usage + cost metrics
  - structured logs with request_id and tenant

### Launch gate criteria (v1)
A template is “launch ready” when it has:
- Passing end-to-end CI smoke tests against staging
- Telemetry contract conformance (automated validation)
- Security review approval for secrets/tool patterns
- Docs walkthrough verified against repo (snippet drift checks)
- Importable dashboard bundle (“observability pack”) verified in Console

---

## Template contract (consistency across languages)
This is the “stable surface area” that templates must adhere to.

### Env var conventions
All templates must support:
- `REDWOOD_API_KEY` (required)
- `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` (optional; defaults to Hosted)
- `REDWOOD_MODEL` (optional; template default documented)
- `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS` (optional; safe default)
- `REDWOOD_MAX_RETRIES` (optional)
- `REDWOOD_TENANT_ID` (optional; for multi-tenant examples)
- `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` / `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (optional; for trace export)

> Exact names and language-specific mapping are tracked in the Template catalog & support matrix.

### Telemetry contract (v1)
Templates must emit:
- **Traces:** request spans with required attributes (request_id, tenant_id, route, model, region, error_class).
- **Metrics:** latency (p50/p95), error rate by class, 429 count, timeout count, token usage + estimated cost.
- **Logs:** structured JSON with request_id, tenant_id, template_name, template_version, error_class, and remediation link (where applicable).

See: “Quickstart telemetry contract v1”.

---

## Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Templates must work on Hosted API by default and provide a clear upgrade path to Dedicated and Private.

### Hosted API (default path)
What templates should demonstrate:
- Simple API key-based auth
- Streaming and non-streaming calls
- Correct handling of common platform errors (429, timeouts, transient network)
- Trace context propagation and request_id correlation so that Console can show:
  - token-level cost breakdown
  - latency by route/model
  - error class and exemplar traces

Recommended user path:
1) Run locally against Hosted.
2) Import dashboards/alerts bundle.
3) Use Console to validate latency/cost/error behavior.

### Dedicated (reserved capacity)
What templates should highlight (guidance + optional config):
- Pinning a model/version aligned with reserved capacity
- Recommended concurrency limits and batching considerations
- Regional routing expectations (avoid region/model mismatch)
- Operational notes for predictable throughput (timeouts sized to expected queueing)

When to recommend Dedicated:
- Sustained traffic with latency SLOs
- Data isolation needs
- Predictable throughput requirements

### Private (VPC / on-prem)
What templates should highlight (guidance + minimal manifests):
- Network boundary considerations (egress rules, internal DNS)
- Key management integration points (KMS/HSM guidance where relevant)
- Audit log expectations and retention pointers
- Safe handling of PII (explicit “do not log” guidance; redaction strategies)

When to recommend Private:
- Regulated workloads
- Strict data residency / isolation
- Air-gapped or constrained networking environments

---

## Safe defaults (review checklist summary)
All template PRs must explicitly review the following:
- **Timeouts:** present and documented; sized to avoid indefinite hangs.
- **Retries/backoff:** enabled only where safe; honors `Retry-After` for 429; bounded attempts.
- **Rate limiting:** graceful handling of 429; provides user-facing guidance.
- **Streaming robustness:** handles disconnects and partial streams; avoids infinite reconnect loops.
- **Tool calling:** allow-list enforced; tool timeouts and output schema validation; safe error propagation.
- **Input validation:** size limits on user inputs and document ingestion payloads.
- **Logging hygiene:** structured logs; no secrets; no raw prompts with PII by default.
- **Secrets:** .env guidance; no secrets in repo; secret scanning enabled in CI.

---

## Rollout and versioning
- Templates are versioned independently of the core API.
- We publish:
  - semantic version tags
  - a changelog summarizing behavior changes
  - a compatibility note with minimum SDK versions (Python/TypeScript)

Versioning principles:
- Breaking changes require a major version bump.
- Telemetry contract changes must be backward compatible where possible; otherwise require a coordinated major version.

---

## Support and escalation
- Known issues + workarounds are tracked centrally and linked from template READMEs.
- Each template must include:
  - “Troubleshooting” section with common failure modes
  - pointer to error taxonomy
  - how to capture trace/log bundles for support

Primary support contacts (internal):
- DevEx on-call rotation (launch week + ongoing)
- Support insights: Dev Patel
- Escalation/supportability: Owen Phillips

---

## Timeline (current plan)
- Discovery & requirements: 2025-11 to 2025-12
- Design & contract definition: 2025-12
- Implementation: 2025-12 to 2026-01
- Pilot & hardening: 2026-01
- Launch: 2026-02
